history.period: 1915 (origins in flood relief); affiliated with Belur Math 15 Feb 1939
history.summary: A branch centre of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission (Vedanta tradition) at N S Avenue, Silchar. Its origins lie in 1915, when monks' flood-relief work in flood-ravaged Cachar inspired local youth to form the Ramakrishna Seva Samiti under Kamini Kumar Chanda (Belur Math's own page says the Sevashrama was 'started in Silchar in 1924' — a discrepancy; affiliation with Belur Math on 15 Feb 1939 is agreed by both sources). Activities include a students' home for tribal boys, coaching centres, a vocational training centre, a library, a mobile medical unit, eye and dental camps, and the Ma Sarada Charitable Dispensary. Assam's Chief Minister inaugurated a newly built Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsadeva here in March 2025, announcing Rs 5 crore for the hospital and Rs 4 crore for the temple's outstanding construction debt. NOT A CONVENTIONAL TEMPLE: it is a monastic/service institution with a worship hall and temple; keep-or-drop decision needed for a temples list.

name: Ramakrishna Mission, Silchar
town_description: Silchar is the headquarters of Cachar district in southern Assam's Barak Valley, on the banks of the Barak (Surma) River. A predominantly Bengali-speaking commercial and educational hub, it is the gateway to Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura, served by an airport, railway station, and national highways.

travel.airport: Silchar Airport (Kumbhirgram, IXS), about 20 km away
travel.railway: Silchar Railway Station (SCL), about 2-3 km away
travel.road: N S Avenue (R K Mission Road), central Silchar; reachable by auto-rickshaw and city transport

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Durga Puja is celebrated by the ashrama
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not formally published — the ashrama generally follows monastic hours with morning and evening worship (Aratrikam); contact the ashrama before visiting.
